text:
Ava Li: kicked off PTQ smoke for redwood-rerank-v2 on full dev split. quick numbers: NDCG@10 -0.9pt, MRR -1.4pt vs fp32 baseline.
Ben R.: can you paste the command and config? per-channel or symmetric? clipping?
Ava Li: ran standard PTQ pipeline, per-channel by default. command:
```
python eval_rerank.py --model redwood-rerank-v2 --quant ptq --scheme per-channel --calib-samples 1024 --batch 64 --clip 99.999 --seed 42 --tokenizer v3.1 --out results/ptq-smoke.json
```
Carmen P.: thanks. any slice breakdown? even a CSV of per-slice diffs would help.
Ava Li: uploaded a short summary. largest drops concentrated in two slices: longform_queries (query_len>80): ndcg@10 -2.8, mrr -3.5; code_snippets (queries containing code backticks / <code> tags): ndcg -3.6, mrr -4.2. small short queries (<8 tokens) slightly improved (+0.3 ndcg).
Dmitri: hmm. that pattern points at tokenization+quant errors amplifying over longer KV cache/sequences. did calibration include enough long/code examples?
Ava Li: not really. calibration set was drawn uniformly from dev. I did a targeted calibration ablation where I replaced 50% of calib samples with longform/code and the code_snippets drop reduced to mrr -2.9 (so ~1.3pt improvement).
Ben R.: interesting. what about clipping strategy? minmax vs percentile?
Ava Li: I tried clip=99.999 and 99.9. 99.9 made longform slightly worse but code slice slightly better. per-channel->symmetric switch cut variance on short queries but increased overall drop by ~0.2pt.
Carmen P.: do we have per-layer activation histograms? any outlier heads?
Ava Li: per-layer activations look okay, but attention logits in early layers show heavier tails for long inputs. suspicious for exponent overflow / softmax sensitivity after quant.
Dmitri: suggestions: 1) run per-slice calibrated PTQ (we just saw benefit), 2) try percentile clipping tuned per-layer (99.9 for early layers), 3) small QAT smoke (1 epoch) on the two failing slices with ranking loss, 4) consider mixed-precision fallback for >80 token queries if latency/cost trade-off allows.
Carmen P.: and add a bring-up guard: if any slice MRR drop >2.0 then auto-run targeted-calib + QAT-smoke and flag model for manual review before PTQ release.
Ben R.: also record tokenizer pipeline details (html strip, whitespace collapse, punctuation normalization). we had a tokenization edge last month that shuffled code punctuation.
Ava Li: noted — run metadata will include seed=42, tokenizer=v3.1, token_pipeline=[lowercase,strip_html,collapse_whitespace], clip=99.999, scheme=per-channel. I'll attach the CSV diffs + per-layer histograms to the run artifact.
EvalBot: automatic summary: ptq_smoke complete. overall_ndcg_delta=-0.9; overall_mrr_delta=-1.4; worst_slice=code_snippets(mrr=-4.2); actions=["run-slice-targeted-calib","ablate-symmetric-vs-per-channel","qat-1-epoch-smoke","add-bring-up-guard"]
Ava Li: i'll run two follow-ups today: (A) per-channel->symmetric ablation with same calib samples and (B) targeted calibration where 50% of samples are longform/code. will post commands and artifacts. :thumbsup: 
Ben R.: please include ran seed and exact tokenizer artifact. if the punctuation normalization differed we need to repro with the previous tokenizer.
Dmitri: add a small diagnostic: sample 200 code queries and strip punctuation, then compare rank flips — call it "punctuation sensitivity" test. if >10% flips on code slice -> fail PTQ.
Ava Li: good call. i'll add that test to the smoke harness and upload diffs. expected next posts in thread with ablation results.
